Subject: Exploring private hosting + on-prem failover

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. BlueHaven is evaluating a private hosting approach where primary traffic would be served from a VPC-hosted Redwood instance in our preferred cloud region, but we need an on-prem failover option for a small subset of telemetry and critical inference in the event of cross-region outage.

High level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood deliver a VPC-hosted primary with an on-prem failover appliance that can be triggered automatically or manually?
- What does the minimum on-prem hardware look like?
- Rough estimate for integration effort and timeline for a pilot (POC) with ~10M tokens/day steady-state with spikes to 50M tokens/day for short bursts.

I attached a short requirements doc and a rough network sketch. Procurement will likely want a two-stage commercial path (pilot pricing, then reserved commit).

Appreciate any initial thoughts. Happy to jump on a call next week.

Best,
Glen

Subject: Re: Exploring private hosting + on-prem failover — preliminary constraints

Quick notes from an infra feasibility perspective. I reviewed the attached sketch and the requirements doc. High level — this is doable but there are clear trade-offs.

Minimum on-prem hardware (PV1 minimal failover):
- 2x NVIDIA A10 GPUs (or equivalent), 512GB RAM, 8 vCPUs per node
- 2-node cluster for basic HA (active-passive for KV cache holdover)
- 100Gbps uplink to customer switch (we can work with lower bandwidth if model warm/cache size is reduced)
- Local SSD for model shards (NVMe, >= 2TB)

Operational constraints and notes:
- Automated failover: we can provide a control-plane orchestrated failover, but it requires a secure, low-latency control-channel between VPC control plane and on-prem appliance (we will need VPN / dedicated interconnect; policy + health checks).
- Cold-start cost: bringing a full model warm on-prem could take 10–30 minutes depending on model variant and quantization; recommend lightweight warmed cache strategy (prefix caching) to reduce RTO to ~3–5 minutes for critical routes.
- Quantization: recommend an int8 variant for the on-prem footprint; this will save memory but requires validation against customer prompts for quality regressions.

Resourcing estimate (for an 8-week POC):
- 0.5 FTE product lead (integration owner)
- 1.0 FTE infra engineer (on-call / setup)
- 0.5 FTE SRE for runbooks & playbooks
- 0.3 FTE security reviewer (to sign off networking/KMS)
- 1 week of partner field engineering (customer site support)

I've attached a quick resourcing spreadsheet (resourcing_estimate_spreadsheet.xlsx) with hour estimates.

Open items for customer:
- Confirm preferred on-prem hardware vendor and whether they can provide a DMZ/bastion for control plane reachability.
- Clarify which routes must fail over (full traffic vs critical subset).

If we move forward, I'll draft a minimal requirements checklist and a pilot runbook. Happy to present at the Thursday sync.

— Karthik

Thanks Karthik — that's helpful and aligns with what I expected. From an Ops/delivery perspective: 

Pilot staffing and timeline (8-week POC):
- Week 0–1: procurement & contract (pilot SOW + pilot discount) — need procurement owner from BlueHaven
- Week 1–2: hardware staging & network validation (on-prem test harness) — we send field engineer on site for 3 days
- Week 3–4: control-plane integration, VPN + auth, initial model warm-up (prefix cache)
- Week 5–6: failover testing (simulated outage), performance tuning and SLO validation
- Week 7–8: acceptance tests, runbook handoff, and pilot retro

Staffing for delivery:
- Delivery lead (0.5 FTE) — Redwood account owner (Olga to lead customer comms)
- Infra engineer (1.0 FTE) — Karthik listed above
- SRE (0.5 FTE) — runbooks and on-call setup
- Security reviewer (ad-hoc) — to validate KMS and access controls

Commercial asks for procurement:
- Pilot price (4–6 weeks): propose 60% of list for pilot work + one-time on-site eng day charges.
- If BlueHaven signs reserved commit after pilot, apply pilot fees to committed spend.

Glen/procurement — can you confirm decision owner for procurement and the preferred PO cadence? Also confirm whether BlueHaven prefers a ring-fenced IP allowlist or dedicated interconnect.

I'll bring a compact SOW template to the sync.

— Hannah
